Quick ops summary from the first triage:
- Observed request queueing on one of the dedicated GPU pools serving NMB checkout; one instance showed elevated memory churn and a restart event at 08:18 PDT.
- When that instance restarted clients were redistributed to warm nodes which appear to have saturated their NVCache and fallen back to a slower codepath (increased tokenization + CPU path for short sequences).
- Error spikes (5xx) correlate with the restart window and an increase in concurrent batched requests during the promotion burst.

I’ve attached the request log slice around the incident window (redwood_request_log_20270604.json). Initial mitigation attempted: reprovisioned + allowed autoscaler to add 2 extra nodes (scaling in progress).

Proposed near-term mitigations (next 30–60m):
1) Force a rolling replacement of the degraded instance (to remove corrupt cache).
2) Temporarily lower batch sizes on checkout route to reduce per-request latency.
3) If warranted, route the checkout endpoint to the stable model variant optimized for low latency (we can fail open to cached responses for low-severity prompts).

I’ll keep updating every 10 minutes.

Marissa

Date: Fri, Jun 4, 2027 at 12:05 PM -0700
Subject: Re: Production: latency up / throughput down on checkout API

Operational update / mitigation steps enacted: 
- Autoscaler added 2 nodes ~11:40 PT; one node was failing health checks and was force-terminated and replaced.
- Rolling replacement completed for the affected pool at 11:58 PT; NVCache warmed on new nodes.
- Decreased checkout batch size from 16->8 for the hot routes to reduce tail latency while nodes stabilize.
- Enabled fallback to the low-latency model variant for high-priority checkout keys; this preserves throughput for the critical path.

Impact timeline & expectations:
- Observed p95 improving from 1.7s -> ~380ms within 15 minutes of the rolling replacement.
- Error rate dropped from 2.3% -> 0.4% after routing change and node replacement.
- We will monitor for recurrence over the next 4 hours; full normalization expected in 30–45 minutes barring new load spikes.

Notes for comms: If recovery holds, recommend the following customer update: 1) short summary of what happened, 2) what we did to mitigate, 3) action items (postmortem + preventive plan), 4) offer of operational credits if SLA threshold breached.
